basic_information.name: Weaviate
basic_information.creator: Weaviate B.V. (founded by Bob van Luijt and Etienne Dilocker, Amsterdam, Netherlands)
basic_information.description: Weaviate is an open-source, cloud-native vector database written in Go that stores both objects and vectors, enabling hybrid search combining dense vector similarity with keyword (BM25) filtering, structured metadata queries, and built-in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) in a single query interface. It features native multi-tenancy, modular vectorizers and rerankers, GraphQL and REST APIs, and supports scaling to billions of objects. As an EU-based company with SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications, it is a strong option for GDPR-conscious European startups building AI-powered search, recommendation, and generative AI applications.
basic_information.release_date: First created in 2016; current latest version is v1.35 (December 2025)
basic_information.license: Open-core: core database is BSD-3-Clause; enterprise features and managed cloud are proprietary

technical_architecture.architecture_type: Cloud-native, distributed, storage-based. Uses a persistent storage engine with HNSW graphs held in memory for fast ANN search. Supports horizontal scaling via sharding and replication. Multi-tenancy is built into the core architecture with per-tenant shards and dynamic tenant state management (ACTIVE/INACTIVE/OFFLOADED). Supports serverless, dedicated cloud, and self-hosted deployments.
technical_architecture.language: Go (core database), with client SDKs in Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, and Go
technical_architecture.embedding_dimensions: Configurable; supports arbitrary embedding dimensions. Commonly used with 384, 768, 1024, 1536-dimensional vectors. No hard upper limit documented.
technical_architecture.indexing_algorithm: HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) as primary vector index, with flat index option for smaller datasets. Supports Product Quantization (PQ), Binary Quantization (BQ, up to 32x memory reduction), and Rescored Quantization (RQ) for memory optimization. Flat index with RQ quantization became GA in v1.35. The ef parameter controls recall/speed tradeoff.
technical_architecture.scalability: Scales to billions of objects. Supports horizontal scaling via sharding across nodes, configurable replication factor for fault tolerance, and native multi-tenancy with per-tenant shards. The Tenant Controller dynamically manages tenant states (ACTIVE, INACTIVE, OFFLOADED) based on workload demand, enabling efficient resource usage for thousands of tenants. Below ~50M vectors runs efficiently on moderate hardware; at very large scale may require more memory/compute than some competitors.
technical_architecture.deployment_options: Weaviate Cloud Shared (formerly Serverless), Weaviate Cloud Dedicated (formerly Enterprise), Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC), self-hosted via Docker, Kubernetes (Helm charts), and embedded Weaviate for development. Available on AWS, GCP, and Azure marketplaces.

rag_specific_capabilities.retrieval_method: Dense vector search (HNSW), sparse keyword search (BM25F), and hybrid search combining both via configurable fusion algorithms (Reciprocal Rank Fusion or RelativeScoreFusion). Vector and BM25 searches run in parallel, then results are fused with configurable relative weights. Also supports GraphQL-based filtered vector search with structured metadata predicates.
rag_specific_capabilities.chunking_strategy_support: Weaviate itself does not perform chunking — it stores and indexes vectors/objects. Chunking is handled upstream by integration partners: LlamaIndex provides semantic, recursive, sentence-based, and document-structure-aware chunking; LangChain offers fixed-size, recursive, and semantic chunking. Weaviate's named vectors feature allows storing multiple vector representations per object (e.g., chunk-level and document-level), supporting hierarchical retrieval patterns.
rag_specific_capabilities.reranking_support: Built-in reranking module that uses a secondary cross-encoder model to reassess and reorder initially retrieved results. Supports pluggable reranker modules including Cohere Rerank, Voyage AI reranker, and custom rerankers. Reranking can be applied as part of the query pipeline without additional external tooling.
rag_specific_capabilities.multimodal_support: Supports multimodal embeddings via pluggable vectorizer modules: img2vec-neural for images, multi2vec-clip for image-text, multi2vec-bind for image/audio/video/text. Weaviate v1.35 introduced multimodal document embeddings via Weaviate Embeddings service. Supports storing and searching across text, images, and other modalities in the same collection.
rag_specific_capabilities.graph_rag_support: Weaviate provides a GraphQL API that enables relationship-based queries alongside vector search. Blog posts and documentation describe combining vector search-based RAG with Graph RAG for hybrid retrieval that leverages both semantic similarity and data relationships. However, Weaviate is not a native graph database — graph-like traversals are achieved through cross-references between objects and filtered queries, not full knowledge graph construction.
rag_specific_capabilities.citation_grounding: No native citation/grounding verification built into the database. Weaviate's generative search (RAG) module returns the source objects alongside generated responses, enabling downstream citation. Grounding and faithfulness evaluation require external tools (e.g., RAGAS, LangSmith evaluators).
rag_specific_capabilities.context_window_optimization: No built-in context window compression or summarization. Weaviate returns ranked results that can be truncated to fit context windows. Named vectors and multi-vector support enable storing summaries alongside full content. Context window management is typically handled by the orchestration layer (LangChain, LlamaIndex) using Weaviate as the retrieval backend.

performance_and_benchmarks.latency: Single-digit millisecond latencies reported for production workloads. For 1M 768-dim vectors, brute force takes ~23ms; HNSW achieves sub-10ms at high recall. P99 latency depends heavily on ef parameter, dataset size, and quantization. Redis benchmarks showed Redis achieving 1.71x faster latency than Weaviate at equivalent recall levels in multi-client tests.
performance_and_benchmarks.throughput: Thousands of queries per second on moderate hardware (GCP n4-highmem-16 with 16 vCPU, 128GB RAM used in official benchmarks). Higher ef values reduce QPS but improve recall. Exact QPS varies with dataset size, dimensionality, and quantization settings. Competitive but generally behind Qdrant and Redis in pure vector-only throughput benchmarks.
performance_and_benchmarks.accuracy_metrics: Maintains >95% Recall@10 and Recall@100 in official benchmarks while keeping low latency. HNSW ef parameter is the primary knob: higher ef yields better recall at the cost of latency. PQ and BQ reduce memory by 4-32x with modest recall degradation (~1-2% at well-tuned settings).
performance_and_benchmarks.benchmark_results: Official Weaviate ANN benchmarks available at docs.weaviate.io/weaviate/benchmarks/ann. In third-party comparisons (Qdrant benchmarks, Redis benchmarks, Medium reproducible benchmarks), Weaviate performs well but is generally not the fastest for pure vector search — Qdrant and Redis tend to lead in raw QPS and latency. Weaviate's strength is hybrid search where parallel BM25+vector with fusion outperforms pure-vector approaches for real-world RAG workloads.

integration_and_ecosystem.framework_compatibility: First-class integrations with LangChain (dedicated langchain-weaviate package), LlamaIndex (native vector store integration), Haystack, DSPy, Semantic Kernel (Microsoft), CrewAI, n8n, and Dify. Weaviate maintains an extensive integration ecosystem page at weaviate.io/product/integrations.
integration_and_ecosystem.model_compatibility: Modular vectorizer architecture supports: OpenAI (text-embedding-ada-002, text-embedding-3-*), Cohere (embed-v3), Google (PaLM, Gemini), Hugging Face Transformers (any sentence-transformers model), Voyage AI, Contextual AI, JinaAI, and custom models. Generative modules support OpenAI GPT-4/4o, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Mistral, Cohere Command, and open-source models via Ollama and local inference. Weaviate Embeddings is a first-party embedding service introduced in 2025.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_integration_status: Yes — official MCP server available at github.com/weaviate/mcp-server-weaviate (open-source)
integration_and_ecosystem.data_source_connectors: Via integration partners: Airbyte (100+ connectors including Notion, Confluence, Slack, S3, databases), Confluent/Kafka (real-time streaming connector), Unstructured (document parsing), Box, Spark connector. LlamaIndex provides 100+ data loaders (PDF, DOCX, web crawl, APIs). No native first-party connectors for specific SaaS tools — Weaviate relies on the ecosystem.
integration_and_ecosystem.observability_integration: Weaviate exposes Prometheus metrics for monitoring. Integrates with observability platforms through the orchestration layer: LangSmith (via LangChain tracing), Langfuse (via OpenTelemetry), Arize Phoenix, and OpenLLMetry. Weaviate Cloud provides built-in monitoring dashboards for cluster health, query latency, and resource usage.

pricing_and_cost.pricing_model: Open-core model: self-hosted is free (BSD-3-Clause). Cloud pricing based on dimensions stored (objects x vector dimensionality x replication factor), chosen SLA tier, storage, and backups. Regional pricing variations apply. New pricing model effective October 27, 2025 renamed tiers: Serverless -> Shared Cloud, Enterprise -> Dedicated Cloud.
pricing_and_cost.free_tier: 14-day free trial for Shared Cloud (formerly Serverless). Self-hosted is free and unlimited. No permanent free cloud tier (unlike Qdrant's 1GB free forever or Pinecone's free tier).
pricing_and_cost.cost_at_scale: Shared Cloud starts at $25/month per 1M vector dimensions stored. For 1M objects with 1536-dim vectors (OpenAI) = 1.536B dimensions = ~$38.40/month base. Dedicated Cloud provides dedicated resources with guaranteed uptime at higher price points. Exact pricing varies by region and SLA tier. Self-hosted cost is infrastructure only (compute + storage).
pricing_and_cost.total_cost_of_ownership: For cloud: Weaviate pricing + embedding API costs + LLM generation costs + storage/backup fees. For self-hosted: infrastructure (recommend 16+ vCPU, 64-128GB RAM for production), DevOps/SRE team time, embedding costs. Self-hosted can be significantly cheaper at scale but requires Kubernetes expertise. At very large scale (>50M vectors), Weaviate may require more memory than some competitors, increasing infrastructure costs.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Top-tier open-source vector database, competing directly with Pinecone, Qdrant, and Milvus/Zilliz. Strong position in hybrid search and RAG use cases. Differentiator is the combination of hybrid search, built-in RAG modules, multi-tenancy, and EU provenance. Market challenger to Pinecone (the managed-first leader) and a peer to Qdrant and Milvus in the open-source segment.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: Instabase (enterprise document automation for financial institutions, insurance, government), Stack AI (enterprise AI agent platform), Kapa AI (technical documentation chatbots, customers include Docker, OpenAI, Monday.com, Grafana, Reddit), and numerous enterprise customers in ecommerce (recommendation/search), financial services, and healthcare. Google Cloud partnership (case study published).
adoption_and_market.community_size: ~15,300 GitHub stars, ~1,200 forks, 50,000+ community members (per Weaviate website). Active Slack community and community forum with 200+ messages/week. ~99 employees.
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: Total raised: $67.7M. Series B: $50M (April 2023) at $200M valuation. Earlier rounds: $16M Series A, $1.7M seed. Key investors: Index Ventures, Battery Ventures, New Enterprise Associates (NEA), Cortical Ventures, Zetta Venture Partners, ING Ventures. Series C of $50M reportedly raised (per SalesTools.io, October 2025), though details are less confirmed.
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Main competitors: Pinecone (managed-first, serverless, easiest ops), Qdrant (Rust-based, fastest raw performance, strong filtering), Milvus/Zilliz (billion-scale, most mature at extreme scale), Chroma (lightweight, developer-friendly for prototyping), pgvector (PostgreSQL extension, simplest for existing Postgres users). Weaviate differentiates with: native hybrid search (BM25+vector fusion), built-in generative search/RAG modules, comprehensive multi-tenancy, GraphQL API, EU headquarters (GDPR advantage), and modular vectorizer/reranker architecture.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Weaviate is well-suited for startups building AI-powered search, recommendation, or RAG applications that need hybrid search (combining keyword and semantic retrieval). Best for: (1) Teams of 2-10 engineers building production SaaS with search/RAG features; (2) Startups needing multi-tenancy (each customer gets isolated data); (3) European startups requiring GDPR compliance and EU data residency; (4) Budgets of $0 (self-hosted) to $500+/month (cloud). Less ideal for: solo developers prototyping (Chroma is simpler), teams wanting zero-ops (Pinecone is easier), or billion-scale deployments with limited engineering resources (Milvus/Zilliz may be more proven at extreme scale).
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Start with Weaviate Cloud Shared (managed) for POC and early production — eliminates DevOps burden and costs $25-100/month for moderate workloads. Move to self-hosted (Docker/Kubernetes) when: monthly cloud bill exceeds $500-1000, you need full data control, or you have a DevOps/SRE team. The Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC) option is a middle ground for enterprises wanting managed service on their infrastructure. Self-hosting requires Kubernetes expertise and monitoring setup but can reduce costs 3-5x at scale.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_production: POC: 1-3 days using Weaviate Cloud + LangChain or LlamaIndex. MVP with hybrid search: 1-2 weeks. Production-ready with multi-tenancy, monitoring, and CI/CD: 4-8 weeks. Self-hosted production deployment with Kubernetes: 6-12 weeks including infrastructure setup, load testing, and monitoring. The Query Agent and Cloud Console provide no-code exploration capabilities that accelerate the POC phase.
key_lessons: 1. Hybrid search (BM25 + vector) consistently outperforms pure vector search for real-world RAG applications — Weaviate makes this a first-class feature rather than requiring external orchestration.

2. Multi-tenancy is critical for B2B SaaS startups: Weaviate's native tenant isolation with dynamic state management (ACTIVE/INACTIVE/OFFLOADED) means you can serve thousands of customers efficiently without running separate database instances.
3. Start managed, migrate self-hosted: use Weaviate Cloud Shared to validate product-market fit, then move to self-hosted Kubernetes when unit economics demand it — the open-source core is identical.

4. EU provenance matters for European startups: Weaviate's Amsterdam HQ, SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, GDPR compliance, and HIPAA readiness simplify enterprise sales conversations, especially in regulated industries.
5. The modular vectorizer architecture means you are not locked into one embedding provider — you can swap OpenAI for Cohere or open-source models without changing your database schema or queries.
entrepreneurial_relevance.no_code_interface: Yes — Weaviate Cloud Console provides: (1) Query Agent for natural-language exploration without code, (2) Collections tool for no-code collection management, (3) Explorer tool for GUI-based data browsing and search. Weaviate Workbench provides additional visual tooling. Not a full no-code RAG pipeline builder, but significantly lowers the barrier for exploration and basic operations.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 3 (Framing & managing AI projects — Build vs Buy, RAG architecture decisions) and Session 4 (AI business models — multi-tenancy for B2B SaaS, unit economics of vector databases)

confidence.data_quality: High — information sourced from official Weaviate documentation, GitHub repository, Crunchbase/Tracxn funding data, official blog posts, peer-reviewed benchmark comparisons, and multiple independent technical reviews.
confidence.cross_reference: Funding confirmed across Crunchbase, Tracxn, PRNewswire, and SiliconANGLE. Technical capabilities verified against official docs, GitHub README, and third-party comparison guides (TensorBlue, Firecrawl, AIMulitple, Medium technical reviews). Pricing confirmed via official weaviate.io/pricing page and eesel.ai pricing guide.
confidence.caveats: Series C funding ($50M, October 2025) reported by SalesTools.io but not confirmed by Crunchbase or official press release — may be unverified or conflated with Series B. GitHub stars count is approximate. Benchmark comparisons vary significantly by methodology — Weaviate's own benchmarks vs third-party benchmarks show different relative performance. Pricing model changed October 2025; costs cited reflect the new model but may evolve. The vector database market is rapidly consolidating and features converge quickly across competitors.
confidence.security_posture: Strong security posture: SOC2 Type I and Type II certified, ISO 27001 certified, GDPR compliant, HIPAA compliant (with BAA). Data encrypted in transit (TLS/mTLS) and at rest (AES-256). Role-based access control (RBAC). Customer-managed encryption keys available. Network isolation in dedicated/BYOC deployments. No publicly known major security incidents. Standard vector database attack surfaces apply: potential for embedding inversion attacks (reconstructing data from vectors) and knowledge base poisoning — mitigated by access controls and input validation.
